steps.question: Do the treated-vs-control differentially expressed genes reproduce under an independent count-based method (edgeR QLF) on the same filtered matrix?

caveats: Enrichment inherits the weakness of a 3-vs-3 contrast: a significant pathway rests on the same six samples and is not independent evidence
GO BP sets are heavily nested, so significant hits arrive in correlated blocks — collapse redundant parent/child terms before reporting a count
A 12,000-gene matrix is a partial transcriptome; gene sets whose members are largely absent from the matrix will be under-powered, so report set coverage alongside each result
steps.context: Human liver, drug treatment vs control, n=3 per group. The reference store holds MSigDB 2026.1 human hallmark (50 sets, HGNC symbols) and human GO BP/CC/MF collections, plus human WikiPathways as an alternative symbol-based GMT. Ranked GSEA is preferred over ORA here because a 6-sample design may produce too few FDR-significant genes for over-representation testing to have any power.
steps.question: Which biological programmes — in particular hepatic drug-metabolism and xenobiotic-response programmes — are coordinately shifted in treated versus control liver samples?
constraints: Use only Homo sapiens gene set collections; never substitute the mouse or rat WikiPathways files
Rank on the full DESeq2 result table — do not pre-filter by padj before building the ranking vector
Use the set of genes actually tested in T1S1 as the ORA background universe, never the whole genome
Report NES sign in terms of the treated-vs-control direction defined in T1S1 (positive = up in treated)
steps.description: Take the complete DESeq2 result table from T1S1 (all tested genes, not a thresholded list), map gene identifiers to HGNC symbols and report the mapping rate, collapse duplicate symbols by keeping the entry with the largest baseMean, and build a ranking vector from the Wald statistic (fall back to sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue) only if the statistic column is unavailable). Human hallmark and human GO biological process gene sets are used; the organism of every GMT used is stated and is Homo sapiens
Identifier mapping rate to HGNC symbols is reported, along with the duplicate-collapse rule applied
Top enriched pathways per collection are reported with NES, adjusted p-value, set size and leading-edge genes
Drug-metabolism / xenobiotic-response set results are reported explicitly with their statistics, including when non-significant
ORA is either run with an expressed-gene background and reported, or explicitly skipped with the DE-list size given as the reason
If a required human gene-set file is absent at run time, the step reports which collection was missing and completes with the collections that are present

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control bulk RNA-seq DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq experiment: /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv holds raw integer gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 6 sample columns + 1 identifier column) produced by STAR alignment and featureCounts, and /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv holds 6 rows with a condition column defining 3 drug-treated vs 3 control human liver samples. Because the counts are gene-level integers from featureCounts and not transcript-level estimates from a quantifier such as salmon/kallisto, there is no tximport step and no average-transcript-length offset: the matrix is loaded directly into DESeq2 with a ~condition design and DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors handle library-depth normalisation. That fact drives step T1S1.

T1S1 does QC and modelling in one pass: verify sample IDs in the count header match metadata rows and align them, confirm counts are non-negative integers, drop genes with near-zero counts using an edgeR filterByExpr-style low-count filter (min group size 3), compute VST for sample-level QC (library sizes, PCA, sample-sample correlation), then fit DESeq2 with design ~condition and extract the treated-vs-control contrast with control as reference. With n=3 per group, dispersion estimation is thin and Wald p-values are the only defensible statistic; LFC shrinkage (apeglm) is applied for ranking and visualisation only, while significance comes from the unshrunken BH-adjusted p-values. T1S2 is a diagnostics and reporting step: p-value histogram, MA and volcano plots, and an independent-filtering summary, so the DE result can be judged rather than taken on faith — including the honest outcome that a 3v3 design may yield few or no genes at FDR 0.05.

T1S3 is a robustness cross-check with edgeR quasi-likelihood on the same filtered matrix. It is cheap and directly addresses the main risk of n=3: that a handful of hits are method-specific artefacts. Concordance between DESeq2 and edgeR-QLF is reported as a confidence qualifier, not as a second discovery pass.

T2S1 takes the full DESeq2 result — ranked by the Wald statistic, not thresholded — into GSEA (fgsea) against human hallmark and GO biological process gene sets, which are present in the reference store for Homo sapiens. Ranked GSEA is the right call here precisely because a 3v3 DE list may be too short for over-representation testing; if the FDR-significant gene list is large enough (>=50 genes) an ORA is added as a secondary readout. Liver tissue means drug-metabolism and xenobiotic-response programmes (CYP/NR1I2/AhR-linked hallmark sets) are the biologically expected axis, and the step is instructed to report those explicitly alongside anything else that surfaces. Gene identifiers in counts.csv are of unstated type, so both DE and enrichment steps must detect the identifier space and map to HGNC symbols before touching the symbol-based GMT files, reporting the mapping rate.
